title: Southern Han
capsule: The Southern Han (917–971) was one of the Ten Kingdoms that emerged from the collapse of Tang, established by Liu Yan at Guangzhou (Xingwang Fu) after declaring himself emperor in 917. Its territory comprised Guangdong, Guangxi, and Hainan, making it a maritime-oriented state well positioned for trade with Southeast Asia and the Arab world. Two attempts to extend power northward into Vietnamese territory — at the Bạch Đằng River in 931 and 938 — both failed, the second crushed decisively by Ngô Quyền, permanently blocking southward Song expansion. The Song dynasty absorbed the Southern Han in 971 when Emperor Houzhu (Liu Chang) submitted to Song forces.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial boundaries are reasonably well established from Song-era historical sources; the precise extent of tributary relationships with upland peoples in Guangxi is less certain.
